findings.message: The client-supplied file name is interpolated into a shell command run with shell=True. A name like `x; rm -rf ~` executes arbitrary commands on the server.
findings.suggestion: subprocess.run(["convert", str(UPLOAD_DIR / client_name), "-resize", "128x128", str(UPLOAD_DIR / target)], check=True)

findings.message: `client_name` is never validated, so names containing `../` or an absolute path escape `UPLOAD_DIR`. This lets a client read arbitrary images and write thumbnails outside the upload directory. Resolve the paths and check that they stay under `UPLOAD_DIR`, or reject any name that is not a plain basename.

Even without a shell, a name starting with `-` is parsed by ImageMagick as an option. ImageMagick coder prefixes such as `msl:` or `text:` can also read or write unintended files. Restrict names to a safe pattern before calling `convert`.
This adds new behaviour without a test, and the repository requires one for every behaviour change.
